name: Slapjack
description: Slapjack (or 'Slaps') is a children's card game that tests speed and reflexes. Players take turns flipping cards onto a central pile. When a Jack appears, the first player to slap the pile wins all the cards in the center. The goal is to collect the entire deck.

overview.description: Slapjack (or 'Slaps') is a children's card game that tests speed and reflexes. Players take turns flipping cards onto a central pile. When a Jack appears, the first player to slap the pile wins all the cards in the center. The goal is to collect the entire deck.

history.origins: Dates back to the 19th century as 'Beggar My Neighbor' variant. The physical act of slapping makes it a perennial favorite for kids.
timeline: Present: A rite of passage for siblings.
history.cultural: Often results in red hands and minor arguments over who was fastest.
history.evolution: Rules like 'Double Slap' (slapping doubles like 6-6) add complexity.

setup.players: Two to eight players; sources recommend about 4–10 for best play. Each player holds their cards as a face-down pile and takes turns flipping to a center pile. Play proceeds clockwise.
setup.deck: One standard 52-card French deck. The pack is divided roughly equally between all players; everyone holds their cards as a face-down pile. No jokers or extra cards are used.
setup.dealing: Deal entirely to players face-down into personal piles.

rules.objective: Collect the entire deck by winning the center pile when a Jack is played. The first player to slap the center pile when a Jack appears wins the pile and adds it to the bottom of their face-down stack.
rules.gameplay: The pack is divided roughly equally between players; each holds cards as a face-down pile. Going clockwise, each player places the top card of their pile face up in the centre. When a Jack is played, the first player to slap the pile wins the centre pile and adds it face down to the bottom of their pile; play continues from the left of the winner. Do not peek at your card before turning it; everyone must see it at once. False slap: if you slap when the top card is not a Jack, you give your top card to the player who played that card. If you run out of cards, you may still slap the next Jack to re-enter; if you fail or false-slap, you are out. The player who has all the cards wins.
keyRules: Turn your card so all players see it at once; do not peek in advance.
Only Jacks are slapped; first to slap the pile wins it.
False slap: give your top card to the player who played the wrongly-slapped card.
Run out of cards: one more chance to slap a Jack to re-enter; otherwise you are out.

strategy.basic: Keep your hand hovering near the pile but not blocking the view. Watch for the 'J' index. Don't slap Queens or Kingsâ€”they look similar (face cards).
strategy.intermediate: Rhythm Disruption: Vary the speed of your flip to throw off opponents. Flip fast, then slow.
strategy.advanced: The 'Fake': Pretend to slap to induce a false slap from a jittery opponent.
tips: Slapping too hard is frowned upon.

variations.name: Time limit
variations.description: Set a time limit; the player with the most cards when time runs out wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Time limit only changes win condition; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Double Slap
variations.description: Slap on matching doubles (e.g. 6-6) as well as on Jacks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Adds slap trigger for doubles; no engine overrides documented.

variations.name: Say Slapjack
variations.description: Player must say 'Slapjack!' when covering the pile; if they fail, they do not get the pile. If they say it and the card is not a Jack, the other players divide the pile.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Adds verbal requirement; no engine overrides documented.
